        if pd.isna(r["brought"]) or pd.isna(r["sold"]) or pd.isna(r["price"]):
            issues.append("missing value")
        elif r["sold"] > r["brought"]:
            issues.append("sold more than brought?")
        past = hist[hist["item"] == r["item"]]
        if len(past) and pd.notna(r["price"]):
            usual = past["price"].median()
            if abs(r["price"] - usual) > 0.3 * usual:
                issues.append(f"price unusual (usually {usual:g})")
        if len(past) and pd.notna(r["brought"]) and r["brought"] > 2 * past["brought"].max():
            issues.append("much more than ever before")
        flags.append(", ".join(issues) or "ok")
    return flags


with tab_read:
    st.subheader("Snap your tally after market")
    left, right = st.columns([1, 1.4])
    with left:
        photo = st.file_uploader("Tally photo", type=["jpg", "jpeg", "png"])
        sample = st.selectbox("...or try a sample (simulated) tally",
                              [""] + sorted(p.name for p in (ROOT / "data" / "samples").glob("tally_*.jpg")))
        path = None
        if photo:
            UPLOADS.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            path = UPLOADS / photo.name
            path.write_bytes(photo.getvalue())
        elif sample:
            path = ROOT / "data" / "samples" / sample
        if path:
            st.image(str(path), use_container_width=True)

    with right:
        if path and st.button("Read it with Gemma", type="primary"):
            with st.spinner("Gemma is reading your handwriting (about 20 seconds)..."):
                result = read_tally(str(path))
            st.session_state["reading"] = result
        result = st.session_state.get("reading")
        if result:
            t = result["tally"]
            st.caption(f"Read in {result['seconds']}s by {result['model']} on this laptop. "
                       f"Written as: \"{t['date_as_written']}\", \"{t['market_as_written']}\"")
            rows = pd.DataFrame(t["rows"])[["written_as", "item", "brought", "sold", "price"]]
            rows["check"] = flag_problems(rows, history)
            c1, c2 = st.columns(2)
            market_day = c1.date_input("Market date", value=date.today())
            market = c2.selectbox("Market", sorted(history["market"].unique()))
            st.write("Check and fix anything Gemma got wrong:")
            edited = st.data_editor(rows, num_rows="dynamic", use_container_width=True,
                                    column_config={"item": st.column_config.SelectboxColumn(options=KNOWN_ITEMS),
                                                   "check": st.column_config.TextColumn(disabled=True)})
            c3, c4 = st.columns(2)
            temp = c3.number_input("Max temperature that day (°C)", value=18.0)
            rain = c4.number_input("Rain that day (mm)", value=0.0, min_value=0.0)
            if st.button("Save to my history"):
                units = history.groupby("item")["unit"].first()
                costs = history.groupby("item")["unit_cost"].median()
                new = edited.drop(columns=["written_as", "check"]).dropna(subset=["brought", "sold"])
                new = new.assign(
                    date=market_day.isoformat(), weekday=market_day.strftime("%a"), market=market,
                    unit=new["item"].map(units), unit_cost=new["item"].map(costs),
                    leftover=new["brought"] - new["sold"], sold_out=new["sold"] >= new["brought"],
                    temp_max_c=temp, rain_mm=rain, holiday_week=False, data_source="REAL")
                save_rows(new)
                st.success(f"Saved {len(new)} rows. They will be used in the next forecast.")


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Tab 2: next market -> TabPFN -> load list
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def reason(hist: pd.DataFrame, market: str, item: str, rainy: bool) -> str:
    past = hist[(hist["market"] == market) & (hist["item"] == item)]
    similar = past[(past["rain_mm"] > 5) == rainy].tail(3)
    if similar.empty:
        return ""
    kind = "rainy" if rainy else "dry"
    lo, hi = int(similar["sold"].min()), int(similar["sold"].max())
    sold_out = int(similar["sold_out"].sum())
    note = f"last {len(similar)} {kind} markets you sold {lo} to {hi}"
    if sold_out:
        note += f" (sold out {sold_out}x, so demand was likely higher)"
    return note


with tab_plan:
    st.subheader("What should I load for the next market?")
    markets = sorted(history["market"].unique())
    c1, c2, c3, c4 = st.columns(4)
    market = c1.selectbox("Market", markets, key="plan_market")
    last_day = pd.to_datetime(history["date"]).max().date()
    day = c2.date_input("Date", value=last_day + timedelta(days=7))
    temp = c3.number_input("Expected max temp (°C)", value=18.0, key="plan_temp")
    rain = c4.number_input("Expected rain (mm)", value=0.0, min_value=0.0, key="plan_rain")
    holiday = st.checkbox("Holiday coming up this week")

    # Items this vendor has been selling at this market recently (in season).
    recent = history[(history["market"] == market) &
                     (pd.to_datetime(history["date"]) >= pd.Timestamp(last_day) - pd.Timedelta(days=35))]
    items = sorted(recent["item"].unique())
    items = st.multiselect("Items to bring", sorted(history["item"].unique()), default=items)

    if items and st.button("Make my load list", type="primary"):
        info = history.groupby("item")[["unit", "price", "unit_cost"]].last()
        upcoming = pd.DataFrame([{
            "date": day.isoformat(), "weekday": day.strftime("%a"), "market": market, "item": i,
            "unit": info.loc[i, "unit"], "price": info.loc[i, "price"], "unit_cost": info.loc[i, "unit_cost"],
            "temp_max_c": temp, "rain_mm": rain, "holiday_week": holiday, "data_source": "FORECAST",
        } for i in items])
        both = add_features(pd.concat([history, upcoming], ignore_index=True))
        train = both[both["data_source"] != "FORECAST"]
        target = both[both["data_source"] == "FORECAST"]
        with st.spinner(f"TabPFN {MODEL_VERSION} is forecasting on this laptop..."):
            rec = recommend(train, target)
        rec["why"] = [reason(history, market, i, rain > 5) for i in rec["item"]]
        out = rec[["item", "bring", "unit", "low", "high", "why"]].rename(
            columns={"low": "slow day", "high": "busy day"})
        st.dataframe(out, hide_index=True, use_container_width=True)
        st.caption("'Bring' leans above the typical day for items with a big margin: "
                   "running out costs you more than a leftover.")
        text = "\n".join(f"{r.item}: bring {r.bring} {r.unit}" for r in out.itertuples())
        st.download_button("Download load list", f"Load list for {market}, {day}\n\n{text}\n",
                           file_name=f"load_list_{day}.txt")


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Tab 3: backtest results
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
with tab_bt:
    st.subheader("Would it have saved money? (backtest on SIMULATED data)")
    st.write("For every past market we trained only on earlier weeks, recommended a load, "
             "and replayed what would have sold. Compared with common rules of thumb:")
    files = sorted(DOCS.glob("backtest_v*.csv"))
    files = [f for f in files if not f.stem.endswith("_rows")]
    if not files:
        st.warning("Run `uv run python -m forecast.backtest` first.")
    else:
        pick = st.selectbox("Run", [f.stem for f in files], index=len(files) - 1)
        table = pd.read_csv(DOCS / f"{pick}.csv", index_col=0)
        table.index = table.index.map({
            "stall_sense": "Stall Sense", "last_sold": "Bring what I sold last time",
            "last_brought": "Bring what I brought last time",
            "vendor_actual": "Vendor's own pen-and-paper guess"}.get)
        st.dataframe(table, use_container_width=True)
        st.bar_chart(table[["waste_$", "lost_profit_$"]])

Web search results for query: "how to make a website not look AI generated design tells 2026"

Links: [{"title":"website not look ai generated","url":"https://21st.dev/blog/website-not-look-ai-generated"},{"title":"Jan 9, 2026","url":"https://bolt.new/blog/2026-create-stunning-websites-bolt"},{"title":"How to Fix AI Slop in Web Design, Tell by Tell","url":"https://capitalandcompute.net/blog/fix-ai-slop-design/"},{"title":"How to Stop Your Vibe Coded Website From Looking AI Generated 3a264170dad0804eb2f2ef31591e60ab","url":"https://app.notion.com/p/REDACTED"},{"title":"2026 create stunning websites bolt","url":"https://claw-sight.bolt.host/blog/2026-create-stunning-websites-bolt"},{"title":"16 Website Design Trends Proving That Polished Is the New Generic","url":"https://www.designrush.com/agency/website-design-development/trends/web-design-trends"},{"title":"gist.github.com","url":"https://gist.github.com/NovCog/c3c9d70ddafb3da451ca3d2a316f324d"},{"title":"website design crash course","url":"https://agentfactory.piaic.org/docs/website-design-crash-course"},{"title":"anti ai slop audit","url":"https://www.skills.sh/avnehsbhatia/ultraui/anti-ai-slop-audit"}]

Search results point to a consistent set of fixes for making a site look less like AI output.

- **Replace generic copy with product-specific claims.** One source says the strongest tell is copy that could describe any product, and that a single specific sentence fixes it. Remove the product name and the sentence still works for a CRM, a note app or a database.
- **Show the real product.** The same source says a screenshot or short screen recording of the actual interface is the fastest single change. It beats any hero illustration.
- **Avoid uneven-free feature grids.** Templated sites use three identical feature cards. Real products have uneven features: one that is genuinely better, one that is a workaround, one nobody uses.

Streamlit's own theming options cover most of what you need, so you usually don't have to inject CSS.

- **Set the font in config.toml:** The docs say you can set the main, heading, and code fonts under the `[theme]` table, with a separate `[theme.sidebar]` table for the sidebar. theme.font sets the default font for all text in the app (except inline code and code blocks). theme.headingFont sets the default font for all headings in the app.
- **Use your own font files:** Use [[theme.fontFaces]] tables to load fonts via Streamlit's static file serving. Per the skills guide, font files must be placed in a static/ directory and served through the app—they cannot be arbitrary local file paths. A forum user found the URL needed an "app/" prefix, so the url for self hosted files for my fonts is "app/static/fonts/". The skills guide also notes that changes to fontFaces require a server restart.
- **Google Fonts work too:** A font can be set with a Google Fonts URL in the same config, as in the skills guide's examples.
- **Hosted fonts:** The docs also have a tutorial for externally hosted fonts, but it targets Streamlit versions below 1.50.0, so check which version you run.
- **Why a CSS injection may fail:** In one forum thread, injecting a `body { font-family }` rule via `st.markdown` did not change the font. That is my inference, not something the sources state, but Streamlit's generated elements are not always targeted by a plain body rule, which is one reason the config route is preferred.

## Externally hosted fonts (Google Fonts, Adobe Fonts)

Encode the font as `{font_name}:{css_url}`. If the family name has a space, wrap it in inner quotes.

```toml
[theme]
font = "Lato:https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Lato&display=swap"
codeFont = "'Fira Mono':https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Fira+Mono&display=swap"
```

Externally hosted fonts may send user data, such as IP addresses, to third-party servers. You are responsible for disclosing this to your users.

## Self-hosted fonts

Enable static file serving, declare each file under `[[theme.fontFaces]]`, and place the files in your app's `static/` folder. Self-hosting supports OTF, TTF, WOFF, and WOFF2. Other formats must be hosted externally.

```toml
[server]
enableStaticServing = true

[[theme.fontFaces]]
family = "myfont"
url = "app/static/MyFont-Regular.woff2"
style = "normal"
weight = 400

[[theme.fontFaces]]
family = "myfont"
url = "app/static/MyFont-Bold.woff2"
style = "normal"
weight = 700

[theme]
font = "myfont"
```

Directory layout:

```
project_directory/
├── .streamlit/
│   └── config.toml
├── static/
│   ├── MyFont-Regular.woff2
│   └── MyFont-Bold.woff2
└── streamlit_app.py
```

Each `[[theme.fontFaces]]` entry accepts `family`, `url`, and optional `weight`, `style`, and `unicodeRange`. Variable font files can cover multiple weights in one file.

## Font keys

| Key | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `theme.font` | Default for all text except code |
| `theme.headingFont` | Headings; falls back to `theme.font` if unset |
| `theme.codeFont` | Inline code and code blocks |
| `theme.codeFontSize` | Code block size, in px or rem (e.g., `"0.875rem"`) |
| `theme.baseFontSize` | Root size, as an integer (default 16) |
| `theme.baseFontWeight` | Root weight, multiples of 50 from 100 to 600 |
| `theme.headingFontSizes` / `headingFontWeights` | Settings for `<h1>`–`<h6>` |
| `theme.metricValueFontSize` / `metricValueFontWeight` | Settings for `st.metric` values |

Sidebar overrides go under `[theme.sidebar]` using the same keys (`font`, `headingFont`, `codeFont`, and so on). Unset sidebar values inherit from `[theme]`.

```toml
[theme]
font = "serif"
headingFont = "sans-serif"
codeFont = "monospace"

[theme.sidebar]
font = "sans-serif"
```

Built-in options are `"sans-serif"` (Source Sans), `"serif"` (Source Serif), and `"monospace"` (Source Code).

## Fallbacks

Use a comma-separated list. End with a built-in font as a backup.

```toml
[theme]
font = "'Nunito Sans':https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Nunito+Sans&display=swap, sans-serif"
```

## Not covered on this page

This page does not document `baseRadius`, `borderColor`, `primaryColor`, `backgroundColor`, or `showWidgetBorder`. It only notes that font color options are described in "Customize colors and borders."

content.content:
## `[theme]` keys on this page

**Value formats**
- **Colors:** a CSS named color (`"darkBlue"`), HEX (`"#483d8b"`), RGB (`"rgb(106, 90, 205)"`), or HSL (`"hsl(248, 53%, 58%)"`). Alpha is allowed but usually unnecessary.
- **Booleans:** `true` or `false` (no quotes).
- **Radius:** the page's examples use `"none"` and `"full"`. It doesn't list other options.
- **Base:** `"light"` or `"dark"`.

**Base and app-wide only**
- `base`: sets the default theme. Defaults to `"light"` if any theme option is set without it.
- `showSidebarBorder`: shows or hides the sidebar border.

**Primary, background, and text colors**
- `primaryColor`: accent for hover effects, focus, and selected items.
- `backgroundColor`: app background.
- `secondaryBackgroundColor`: contrast for widget inputs, headers, and code (when `codeBackgroundColor` is unset).
- `textColor`: default text color.
- `linkColor`: Markdown link color.
- `linkUnderline`: boolean, default `true`. The underline matches `linkColor`.
- `codeTextColor`: inline code text.
- `codeBackgroundColor`: code block and inline code background.

**Borders and widget borders**
- `borderColor`: border color for containers, the sidebar, tabs, and buttons. Also used for widget borders when `showWidgetBorder` is on.
- `showWidgetBorder`: boolean. Shows borders on unfocused widgets.

**Radius**
- `baseRadius`: radius for most elements, including buttons, containers, code, and images.
- `buttonRadius`: overrides `baseRadius` for buttons and `st.segmented_control`.

**Dataframe and table**
- `dataframeBorderColor`: overrides `borderColor` for dataframes and tables.
- `dataframeHeaderBackgroundColor`: header background.
- `dataframeHeaderTextColor`: header text and icon color.

**Chart colors**
- `chartCategoricalColors`, `chartSequentialColors`, `chartDivergingColors`: the page doesn't specify their value format.
- Chart series colors can also be set in `[theme.light]` and `[theme.dark]`. Unset sections inherit from `[theme]`.

**Basic color palette**

For each of `red`, `orange`, `yellow`, `green`, `blue`, `violet`, and `gray` (or `grey`), you can set:
- `<name>Color`
- `<name>BackgroundColor`
- `<name>TextColor`

For example: `redColor`, `redBackgroundColor`, `redTextColor`.

"""
Stall Sense: the app. Everything runs on this laptop (Gemma via Ollama,
TabPFN locally). No internet needed after setup.

Run:  uv run streamlit run app/app.py
"""

import sys
from datetime import date, timedelta
from pathlib import Path

import pandas as pd
import streamlit as st

ROOT = Path(__file__).parent.parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT))

from extract.read_tally import KNOWN_ITEMS, read_tally  # noqa: E402
from forecast.config import MODEL_VERSION  # noqa: E402
from forecast.model import add_features, recommend  # noqa: E402

HISTORY = ROOT / "data" / "history.csv"          # the vendor's own data (gitignored)
STARTER = ROOT / "data" / "synthetic" / "SIMULATED_sales_portland_or.csv"

content.text:
I've redesigned the app, and it's running again at **http://localhost:8501**. I checked it with screenshots at desktop and phone width, and saved four of them to `docs/` for the post.

**What I changed, based on the research:**

| Looks AI-made | What Stall Sense does now |
|---|---|
| Purple/blue gradients, colours with no purpose | Newsprint paper and ink. Green means "bring" or money gained; tomato red appears only for waste and warnings. |
| Inter everywhere | Fraunces (a quirky old-style serif) for headings, Bricolage Grotesque for text, JetBrains Mono for numbers. The fonts ship with the app, so it still works offline. |
| Emoji icons, rounded cards with shadows | No emoji, square corners, no shadows. The structure comes from ruled lines and a double rule under the masthead, like a ledger. |
| Vague copy ("AI-powered insights") | "Photograph Saturday's tally. Get Wednesday's load list. Stop guessing how much kale goes in the van." |
| A hero image instead of the product | The load list is the main thing on screen. Each item has a big green number, a slow-to-busy range bar with the recommendation marked, and a reason like "Last 3 dry markets: sold 34–39. **Sold out 1×**". |
| Generic info boxes and charts | The simulated-data warning is a red rubber stamp. The track record is told in one sentence with real numbers, and it also states the extra sellouts. |

**Full backtest result (TabPFN-2, 185 simulated market days):** Stall Sense would have earned **$4,955 more profit (+8.7%)** than the vendor's own guesses and wasted **57% less stock**. It also sold out 130 more times. The app shows that trade-off openly rather than hiding it.

**Still open:**
1. **TabPFN-3.5 license:** accept it on the Licenses tab at ux.priorlabs.ai so I can run the 3.5 comparison.
2. **Commit and push:** can I commit and push to GitHub? Pushing makes the code and the session transcripts public. `.env` and your history file stay private.
3. **Restart VS Code** so that Entire starts recording these sessions.

Sources: [21st.dev](https://21st.dev/blog/website-not-look-ai-generated), [Capital and Compute](https://capitalandcompute.net/blog/fix-ai-slop-design/), [prg.sh on the purple gradient](https://prg.sh/ramblings/Why-Your-AI-Keeps-Building-the-Same-Purple-Gradient-Website), [925 Studios guide](https://www.925studios.co/blog/ai-slop-web-design-guide), [Bolt 2026 guide](https://bolt.new/blog/2026-create-stunning-websites-bolt), [Streamlit fonts docs](https://docs.streamlit.io/develop/concepts/configuration/theming-customize-fonts), [Streamlit colour docs](https://docs.streamlit.io/develop/concepts/configuration/theming-customize-colors-and-borders)
